    #142245. Breaking: Nvidia chip buyers told to rule out Chinese renters to purchase GPUs, sources say

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (460 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Nvidia chip buyers told to rule out Chinese renters to purchase GPUs, sources say

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (460 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Neoclouds are being told they won't be able to purchase Nvidia chips if any of the computing capacity will be rented by Chinese companies, sources told CNBC.
    • In a recent development, it comes after a new rule restricting remote access to artificial-intelligence semiconductors was announced by the Trump administration on Nov.
    • It has been revealed that chip sellers communicated the messaging to neoclouds after the announcement, which seeks to close an export controls loophole allowing Chinese companies to rent access to Nvidia's most advanced chips when hosted in data centers overseas, two people familiar with the situation told CNBC.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Neoclouds are being told they won't be able to purchase Nvidia chips if any of the computing capacity will be rented by Chinese companies, sources told CNBC.

    In a recent development, it comes after a new rule restricting remote access to artificial-intelligence semiconductors was announced by the Trump administration on Nov. 16.

    It has been revealed that chip sellers communicated the messaging to neoclouds after the announcement, which seeks to close an export controls loophole allowing Chinese companies to rent access to Nvidia's most advanced chips when hosted in data centers overseas, two people familiar with the situation told CNBC. The people asked not to be named when discussing private information.

    Industry observers note that the interim final rule was confirmed by the Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, and came into effect on Nov. 19. Previously imposed export controls have effectively banned the sale of the most advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese companies and their import into China.

    Prior to the new rule's announcement, Nvidia had stated it would not sell its chips to customers renting more than 50% of the graphics processing units, or GPUs, to Chinese companies, CNBC reported.

    Industry observers note that the newly introduced rule impacts the full supply chain, from the companies selling Nvidia chips to the neoclouds who rent access to computing power. Neocloud stocks have come under renewed pressure lately as investors questioned the sustainability of the AI boom.

    Industry observers note that nvidia and the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

    Industry observers note that the change has prompted Nvidia chip sellers to look for fresh buyers of the semiconductor giant's GPUs, CNBC reported on Wednesday, citing three people familiar with the matter. Two of those people said it appeared chip sellers were seeking to offload GPUs because they were originally for use in data centers through which Chinese companies would rent access.

    According to recent reports, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday that the fresh BIS rule was intended to close "loopholes.".

    "Some rules were issued by the Commerce Department last week to close off indirect access, either smuggling through places like Southeast Asia or remote access from data centers in third countries," he said.

    In a recent development, U.S. lawmakers have been looking to clamp down on China's access to advanced compute.

    Separately, Nvidia warned its customers that the proposed Remote Access Security Act — which has passed the House of Representatives but is yet to pass the Senate — would give the U.S. government broader authority to control access to cloud services, potentially exposing both parties to "legal action," sources previously told CNBC.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia shares gapped higher at the open by more than 30%, on pace for its biggest one-day gain in 23 years on Monday, following the news just before the bell that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is going to be reinstated.
    • Investors and traders said that while this reflex rally may have more to run, cautiousness is warranted on Nvidia and the AI trade because of the overhang of investigations into the alleged Chinese espionage involving the company and others, as well as the possibility for data center moratoriums as Democrats take control of Congress and key governor posts in January.
    • "Am I as bullish on Nvidia now as I was on Friday?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you blink, you may have missed it.

    Nvidia shares gapped higher at the open by more than 30%, on pace for its biggest one-day gain in 23 years on Monday, following the news just before the bell that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is going to be reinstated.

    Investors and traders said that while this reflex rally may have more to run, cautiousness is warranted on Nvidia and the AI trade because of the overhang of investigations into the alleged Chinese espionage involving the company and others, as well as the possibility for data center moratoriums as Democrats take control of Congress and key governor posts in January.

    "Am I as bullish on Nvidia now as I was on Friday? Of course not, you can't be," remarked Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, which counted Nvidia as its largest position as he bought on the dip over the last few weeks. "I'm trimming back.".

    "All the same concerns that were here before Jensen resigned are still here," he added.

    It has been revealed that the day before Huang resigned on Nov. 12 as CEO, Nvidia closed at $173.73. It's intraday high on Monday was $171.50, up from its recent low around $125 as it was selling off in the wake controversies. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF closed at $506.96 the day before his resignation. It reached a high of $469.35 before losing steam as trading wore on Monday.

    Mike Khouw, YieldMax strategist at Tidal Financial Group, told CNBC on Monday that there were "sighs of relief," "applause" and even "cheering" among investors at the news of Huang's potential reinstatement. But he also mentioned there are still considerable risks facing the AI trade.

    According to recent reports, jensen Huang was not the only problem at Nvidia, he said, and there are still many vulnerabilities in the overall AI trade, which should give investors pause. Credit-sensitive companies are still at risk of faltering, Khouw added.

    The national security implications of the scandal that has rocked Nvidia and the global AI trade more broadly aren't going away any time soon even as the Trump administration assured the Nvidia board there were none. Investors on Wall Street are expressing strategic concerns about ways to play the tech space just as lawmakers in Washington are demanding answers.

    Democrats are demanding answers on what exactly happened with Nvidia and the Chinese government.

    Recent findings suggest that "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the manufacturer's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) noted in a Monday statement. "The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what 'input' was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement.".

    House Ways and Means ranking member Richard Neal (D-Mass.) stressed the importance of Congressional oversight in determining the best course of action to move forward. The outcome of any Congressional investigations will likely be crucial for Nvidia's long-term viability as an investment opportunity, especially since the company does so much international business.

    Industry observers note that "This is an export control issue," Neal told CNBC on Monday. "Congress is not subservient to this president or any other president as it relates to trade and tariff policies. This is a trade related issue.".

    Many of the same Democrats will call for a slowdown in the data center buildout, a strong glitch for the public partly responsible for their Blue Wave earlier this month.

    Sources indicate that "You're going to have to work your way through what these data center moratoriums all mean," said Niles. "Now I think the broader market keeps going but I am not as convinced on the move in the data-center centric names from here.".

    It has been revealed that to be sure, many Wall Street analysts were rushing to upgrade Nvidia's stock on Monday after Huang's reinstatement. Most restored price targets well above $200 with one as high as $270. But many traders think the rebound may fail before getting back to those levels.

    Famed short seller Michael Burry, who made a boatload betting against Nvidia with put options as it cratered, told his Substack audience that he thinks the rebound here could be "outsized," especially with low volume in the market overall because of the Thanksgiving holiday this week.

    But he too sees the rally eventually losing steam.

    It has been revealed that "Jensen being back without much more information might even restore NVDA to the high 100s," Burry wrote. "I won't short it on this information I have today until it gets closer to or maybe hurdles $200.".

    Industry News: Bills beat Chiefs on deflected punt, Tyler Bass' 57-yard field goal at the buzzer

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1441 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Bills overcame a sluggish offensive game in rainy, windy conditions to beat the Chiefs on Thanksgiving in Buffalo, winning 13-10 on Tyler Bass' 57-yard field goal as time expired.
    • Recent findings suggest that the kick came after a Bills defensive stop deep in the Chiefs' own end and a partial block of Matt Araiza's punt.
    • It was Buffalo's sixth straight regular-season victory over the Chiefs, dating back to 2021.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Bills overcame a sluggish offensive game in rainy, windy conditions to beat the Chiefs on Thanksgiving in Buffalo, winning 13-10 on Tyler Bass' 57-yard field goal as time expired.

    Recent findings suggest that the kick came after a Bills defensive stop deep in the Chiefs' own end and a partial block of Matt Araiza's punt. Local hero Joe Andreesen got a piece of Araiza's punt, and Greg Dortch bravely returned it to the Kansas City 39-yard line, setting up Bass' game-winner in an ugly offensive night.

    It was Buffalo's sixth straight regular-season victory over the Chiefs, dating back to 2021.

    According to recent reports, the Chiefs had a chance to run out the clock in a 10-10 game with less than 30 seconds left, but Patrick Mahomes fumbled the first-down snap, derailing the drive, and Travis Kelce dropped a well-placed pass that likely would have sent the game to overtime. The Bills then deflected Araiza's punt and returned it to the Chiefs' 39-yard line.

    The Chiefs also had a huge first-down catch by Rashee Rice controversially wiped out by replay with just under two minutes left that could have tilted the game in Kansas City's favor.

    The two teams combined for 471 yards of offense in the poor weather, which kept up for the duration of the game.

    The Bills moved to 10-1, maintaining their lead on the rest of the AFC. The Chiefs fell to 8-3, half a game behind the first-place Broncos in the AFC West.

    Recent findings suggest that buffalo increased its probability of winning the conference's No. 1 seed to 63%, according to The Athletic. Kansas City's fell to 3%.

    According to recent reports, josh Allen struggled through one of the poorest passing games of his career, throwing for 81 yards and two interceptions. His legs got the Bills out of some jams, but they mainly had to lean on the running of James Cook, who ran for 117 yards and their only touchdown of the game on 32 carries, which tied his career high.

    Mahomes, the hotter quarterback coming into the game, had more success Thursday, throwing for 174 yards on 16-of-29 passing. But the Chiefs punted on their first four possessions and came up empty on their final four series, with Harrison Butker's missed field goal with just over six minutes left looming large.

    Industry observers note that the first half was a mess — cold, rainy, windy — and a stark contrast to the high-scoring first two games on Thanksgiving. Both teams traded a pair of punts in a scoreless first quarter. The Bills struck first, laboring down the field to get in the end zone on Cook's 5-yard run, overcoming an overturned TD and a questionable false-start call at the goal line.

    In a recent development, buffalo's suddenly hot defense took advantage of the elements and KC's four straight punts to open the game. It appeared that the Bills would take a two-score lead as they drove to the Chiefs' 9-yard line, but Allen's pass was tipped by George Karlaftis and intercepted in the end zone by Alohi Gilman to thwart that drive.

    The Chiefs finally got going before halftime, driving to the Bills' 8-yard line, but Mahomes' end-zone pass to Rice was incomplete, and the Chiefs settled for a short Butker field goal to cut Buffalo's lead to 7-3.

    Kansas City came out of halftime with renewed focus, looking the best they had offensively all game. Emmett Johnson, starting again for an injured Kenneth Walker III, capped the drive with a 1-yard TD run. It was an impressive drive despite the rain continuing to fall, giving the Chiefs a 10-7 lead. It was Johnson's fifth straight game with a touchdown. That score ended a streak of 49 drives without allowing a TD by the Bills' defense.

    In a recent development, allen, who had only 41 first-half passing yards, was working through his issues gripping the ball, and the Bills penetrated the Chiefs' red zone on their opening drive of the third quarter. But Allen's on-target pass to Khalil Shakir deflected off his hands and went down as Allen's second interception, this time by Nohl Williams.

    In a recent development, the Bills' defense muscled up again and pushed the Chiefs back, giving Buffalo good field position again. Another labored drive — its fifth of the game of at least four minutes — bogged down, as the Bills had to settle for Bass' 54-yard field goal, tying the game at 10-10.

    Mahomes was under fire on the ensuing drive, but he completed a third-and-15 pass under heavy pressure — vintage Mahomes — throwing back against his body for 19 yards and a clutch first down.

    But penalties were a problem all game for the Chiefs, and consecutive flags pushed them back 15 yards. The Chiefs settled for a Butker field-goal try from 46 yards, but he pushed it to the right for his eighth miss of the season. That is two more than he's had in any single season in his 10 years as a Chief.

    "I'm not going to make any decisions," Reid noted when asked about Butker's struggles, according to The Athletic's Nate Taylor.

    The Chiefs' defense revealed it could flex its muscles, too. After Cook moved the chains, the Chiefs sacked Allen just as the Bills moved into Kansas City territory. It was that kind of night for the offense and for Allen.

    Backed up inside his own 10, Mahomes hit Rice with an 11-yard pass on third-and-10, taking a major hit from the Bills' Amani Hooker. But the play was reviewed, and it was determined that the ball came loose and touched the ground, forcing the Chiefs to punt.

    Allen got the ball back at his 47-yard line with plenty of time to mount a game-winning drive but had a first-down completion wiped out by penalty and took a massive sack on third down, and the Bills punted with less than 40 seconds left in regulation.

    Instead, the Chiefs watched the Bills pull out the ugly game in the waning seconds.

    In a recent development, the Bills won a game in which Josh Allen went 10-for-21 for 81 yards, 0 touchdowns and 2 interceptions. It began as a slog, but then every stop began landing like a haymaker.

    All three games today were decided in the final three seconds.

    In a recent development, tyler Bass is good from 57 yards out and that will do it. This game seemed destined for overtime, until a catastrophic play put the game in the Bills' hands. That missed 46-yarder by Harrison Butker looms large.

    A Chiefs three-and-out, a tipped punt and a quick return has the Bills attempting a 57-yarder for the win.

    Patrick Mahomes fumbled the shotgun snap in the Buffalo cold and rain, but he got the ball back before the Bills defense could get there.

    The Bills appeared to move into field goal position, but Dalton Kincaid got called for a blatant offensive pass interference, then Josh Allen got sacked on 3rd-and-9. The Bills are punting with 38 seconds left.

    According to recent reports, it's a short punt for the Chiefs too. Buffalo will get the ball at the Kansas City 37-yard line needing only a field goal with 1:40 left.

    In a recent development, the Chiefs were facing 3rd-and-10 deep in their own territory, but Patrick Mahomes found Rashee Rice for 11 yards and a first down. However, replay overturns the catch — Rice didn't have the ball secure when it hit the ground — and that makes this a three-and-out for Kansas City.

    The Bills' next drive goes nowhere quickly, with Nick Bolton and Christian Roland-Wallace combining to sack Josh Allen on third down. The Chiefs will get the ball back at their own 9-yard line with two minutes left.

    Harrison Butker lined up for the 46-yard attempt, but his kicking woes continued.

    He was not able to handle the weather conditions and pushed the kick wide right.

    The game remains tied at 10 with 5:56 left in regulation.

    Bad weather isn't keeping Patrick Mahomes from pulling some magic.

    After scrambling toward the right sideline, he threw across his body, and Cyrus Allen came out of nowhere to pick up 19 yards on third and 15.

    The fourth quarter began with Buffalo getting some extra yards, but not being able to sustain the drive.

    Even with the bad weather, Tyler Bass lined up for the 54-yard attempt. He nailed it as it hooked right through the uprights to tie the game at 10.

    12 minutes to go in a brand newly introduced ballgame.

    #142235. Kalshi daily volume of ‘perps’ trading begins to top its prediction markets

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (764 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Kalshi daily volume of ‘perps’ trading begins to top its prediction markets

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (764 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Kalshi is known for its prediction markets across sports, politics and culture.
    • But now, for the first time, perpetual futures, Kalshi's second financial product, has surpassed the notional trading volume of its event contracts on consecutive days.
    • On Thursday, perpetual futures — commonly known as "perps" — on Kalshi saw $3.4 billion in notional volume as artificial intelligence laboratory Anthropic stock debuted on public markets while the rest of the market sold off.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Kalshi is known for its prediction markets across sports, politics and culture.

    But now, for the first time, perpetual futures, Kalshi's second financial product, has surpassed the notional trading volume of its event contracts on consecutive days.

    On Thursday, perpetual futures — commonly known as "perps" — on Kalshi saw $3.4 billion in notional volume as artificial intelligence laboratory Anthropic stock debuted on public markets while the rest of the market sold off. That exceeded about $3 billion in notional volume for Kalshi's prediction markets on the same day.

    Perps are futures-style contracts where there is no expiration and traders do not need to own the underlying asset. Contracts instead continuously track the price of an asset, with funding payments to keep the contract price aligned with that of the market. Funding payments are made periodically between holders of short or long positions.

    Perps trading surpassed event contracts one day in September, but on Friday perps topped prediction markets volume for a second day. Now Kalshi expects that performance to continue as it introduces perps tied to more individual stocks. On Monday, for example, Kalshi introduced contracts linked to Anthropic.

    Sources indicate that kalshi was the first to debut perps in the U.S. after winning federal regulatory approval in May to list perps tied to cryptocurrencies.

    Perps trading volume includes any leverage that speculators acquire along with their trade, while event contracts are fully collateralized — for now.

    Since the original launch in May, Kalshi has received approval to introduce perps tied to metals, crude oil, stock indexes and individual stocks.

    Industry observers note that offshore perps — those available on exchanges not regulated in the U.S. — generated more than $90 trillion in notional trading volume in 2025, so it's not surprising that the product has grown so rapidly on Kalshi, according to Udesh Jha, chief risk officer at Kalshi Klear, the manufacturer's clearing house.

    According to recent reports, "We're just in very early innings. We're launching products, we're growing the participant base.".

    Industry observers note that perps were Kalshi's first product to mark its transition from a prediction market-focused platform to a full-blown financial exchange where various assets are traded. Last week, reports said that Kalshi is planning to offer trading on equities on its platform in the coming months.

    According to recent reports, at the same time, the organization's perps product has come under fire. Some incumbent exchanges where futures are traded — which saw their stock prices decline following the approval of U.S. perps — believe the product was improperly approved. CME Group is suing the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the federal derivatives regulator, for approving perps.

    In a recent development, others have simply expressed concerns about the efficiency of the markets. CNBC previously reported that trading volume on Kalshi's most popular perps markets — tied to bitcoin and ether cryptocurrencies — was dramatically greater than open interest, or cash actively in the markets. It's a phenomenon that isn't common with U.S.-regulated traditional futures, nor other offshore perps markets.

    Kalshi said at the time it has "zero concerns" about the distinction, and that it appears because less leverage is offered compared to offshore exchanges and there are fewer incentives for traders to park capital on its perps markets.

    While Kalshi started with cryptocurrencies, Owen Lau, an analyst at Clear Street, noted perps tied to individual stocks likely represent the most promising opportunity for growth in the U.S.

    Industry observers note that "That's how I foresee the way perps will penetrate further into traditional asset classes," Lau remarked. "Perps on single stocks and [key performance indicators on individual companies] could change how investors hedge their portfolio or even make a directional bet.".

    Industry observers note that kalshi's growth has been powered by the fact that right now it's the only exchange that can actively list perps in the U.S., though crypto exchange Coinbase received approval in May to route U.S. users to offshore platforms for trading. That monopoly status, however, will probably prove short lived.

    Coinbase has filed to list single-stock perps in the U.S., and President Donald Trump in August said the CFTC is working to bring Hyperliquid — a dominant player in offshore perps activity — to domestic traders.

    But Jha at Kalshi isn't worried about the competition.

    "What will carry us is ... making sure that we have the right products for the marketplace, making sure we have the right surveillance of the products that we are trading.".

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

    Fears about the massive debt being taken on to fund the artificial intelligence buildout climbed Tuesday as Wall Street weighed what Huang's return to Nvidia means for its bankrolling of the AI boom.

    Sources indicate that huang is considered one of the top financiers, or bankers, in the AI industry, spearheading deals with neoclouds like CoreWeave and other firms to buy chips, backed in some cases by Nvidia guarantees. His return to Nvidia has revived prospects for the manufacturer to continue "circular financing" of AI chips and data centers — raising concerns among credit investors.

    CoreWeave, which has become the poster child of AI debt concerns, saw its stock sink 13% and the yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 top 17%. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    At the same time, the spread on the neocloud firm's five-year credit default swaps jumped 8.5% to over 1,200 basis points. Credit default swaps are insurance against nonpayment and are considered a barometer of perceived risks. Rising CDS spreads mean investors view the debt as riskier.

    Huang was reinstated as CEO on Monday after stepping down on Nov. 12 amid allegations of multiple affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. His reinstatement on Monday was cheered by investors, who pushed stocks higher, yields lower and spreads on CDS tighter. However, stocks retreated, bond yields rose and CDS spreads widened on Tuesday.

    Ben Emons, founder and chief investment officer at FedWatch Advisors, called it a waning of the "Jensen effect.".

    The moves suggest "markets see government intervention as 'moral suasion' that carries credit and interest-rate risks," he mentioned.

    President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday he "convinced" the board to bring Huang back.

    CoreWeave wasn't the only name seeing heightened concerns in CDS spreads. Oracle's five-year CDS spread jumped 7% to 355.68. Even highly rated hyperscalers Meta Platforms and Amazon.com saw spreads widen by more than 2%. Nvidia's CDS added 3.4%.

    Larry Holzenthaler, senior portfolio manager for fixed income at Catalyst Funds, believes the drama that unfolded with Huang's return to Nvidia won't necessarily sit well with credit investors.

    According to recent reports, "A lot of old school credit people are going to look at what kind of materialized there, the administration's involvement in putting him back in, and I think a lot of credit participants are going to step back and tiptoe away from that a bit," he stated. "Credit market investors typically don't like that type of drama or uncertainty.".

    According to recent reports, while Nvidia has commitments across the AI ecosystem, it is the neoclouds that have been under the most scrutiny. Many of the companies, which rent out AI computing power and cloud capacity, are highly leveraged and have relied on Nvidia financing to reduce their exposure to the bond market.

    With so much riding on Nvidia's funding, Huang's next move is being closely watched.

    During his brief absence, chief financial officer Colette Kress noted during the company's earnings call that Nvidia would be "rigorously evaluating future investments" and will remain disciplined in how it commits capital.

    That suggested Nvidia was going to be more judicious with financing, says Paul Meeks, head of technology research at Freedom Capital Markets.

    "That concern should be put to rest with Jensen [Huang] back," he said.

    Investor Steve Eisman, of "Big Short" fame and host of "The Real Eisman Playbook" podcast, believes Huang feels emboldened now that he's back in charge.

    "[H]e'll double down on the circular financing," Eisman predicted on CNBC's "Squawk Box" Tuesday.

    After Huang's departure, Eisman believed that the ecosystem the CEO created by pouring money into AI companies would likely unwind and leave some of the companies in "substantial trouble.".

    "Now that he's back, they're not," he said.

    Others are not so certain the level of funding will continue.

    "Given scrutiny of disclosure around financing and guarantees … we do not expect Mr. Huang's return to bring a quick reversion to broader customer financing," Stifel analyst Ruben Roy said in a note Monday.

    Nvidia stated on its earnings call that it has $118 billion in guarantees, as of Oct. 25, to back AI projects.

    Concerns about the level of debt to fund the AI infrastructure buildout had already taken hold before Huang's departure and reinstatement.

    "These complications have not disappeared just because the White House pressured the weak board to reinstate Jensen Huang," stated economist David Rosenberg, founder and president of Rosenberg Research.

    John Lloyd, global head of multi-sector and corporate credit at Janus Henderson Investors, believes having Huang back at the helm "reaffirms his existing go-to-market strategy." However, the credit market is still taking a cautious look at the neoclouds as it waits for more clarity on long-term supply/demand dynamics.

    Still, Lloyd is cautiously positive on CoreWeave, which he owns in portfolios he manages, and noted all the data point to a "pretty healthy environment right now." That includes strong residual values on graphics processing units and spot compute rates, he noted.

    "The company is doing everything in its power to execute," he mentioned. "They don't need the high yield market at this time.".

    In a recent development, in the meantime, investigations into Nvidia and Huang are ramping up. Huang is expected to appear before three House committees next week. Nvidia is conducting an independent investigation into his activities, and California Attorney General Rob Bonta has launched a probe. At the federal level, President Trump mentioned Monday that U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche "has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.".

    Recent findings suggest that "There's other shoes to drop," Rosenberg said. "I don't think that the book has been closed on this file.".

    #142226. U.S. tariff-hike threats pile pressure on partners to sign trade deals

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1562 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    U.S. tariff-hike threats pile pressure on partners to sign trade deals

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1562 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Trump administration has unveiled a fresh tariff salvo on more than a dozen trading partners, with China, Vietnam, and India facing some of the steepest potential rates and mounting pressure to conclude trade deals with Washington.
    • The proposed tariffs, framed as curbing excess industrial capacity, start at 15% for the European Union, South Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan and rise to as much as 35% for Vietnam.
    • Trade Representative's Office said it intends to cap the new duties at lower levels for countries that have completed trade deals or are still negotiating with Washington.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Trump administration has unveiled a fresh tariff salvo on more than a dozen trading partners, with China, Vietnam, and India facing some of the steepest potential rates and mounting pressure to conclude trade deals with Washington.

    The proposed tariffs, framed as curbing excess industrial capacity, start at 15% for the European Union, South Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan and rise to as much as 35% for Vietnam.

    It has been revealed that the U.S. Trade Representative's Office said it intends to cap the new duties at lower levels for countries that have completed trade deals or are still negotiating with Washington.

    The overall impact on the region is likely to be limited, mentioned Mark Williams, chief Asia economist at Capital Economics. The proposal "puts most of the targeted countries back where they were earlier in the year," he said, after the Supreme Court struck down Trump's emergency tariffs in February.

    Still, the proposal could give some countries an incentive to speed up trade talks in order to lock in lower tariff rates, analysts said.

    According to recent reports, on Wednesday, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said that the new policy likely will not take effect for months, with a senior U.S. official saying the duties could take effect as early as January.

    China faces a capped rate of 20%, on top of an existing 25% tariff imposed during President Donald Trump's first term. The rate could rise to 40% if the trade truce reached in South Korea last October is not extended beyond January, the USTR said.

    Beijing has rejected Washington's claim of excess capacity while vowing to take measures necessary to protect its rights.

    On Thursday, Chinese Commerce Ministry spokesperson He Yadong called on Washington to "rectify its wrongdoing and return to the right track of resolving issues through dialogue.".

    Recent findings suggest that he was responding to Washington's plan to raise tariffs following its Section 301 investigations, while the ministry also urged the U.S. to implement $30 billion of reciprocal tariff cuts agreed by the two sides in late September.

    The renewed tensions come despite several conciliatory meetings between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping this year, as well as what Williams described as Trump's "apparent lack of concern" about allegations that Chinese technology firms have circumvented U.S. chip export controls.

    The two leaders are expected to meet for a fourth time this year at the Group of 20 leaders summit in Miami in December.

    "While not happy, Beijing seems prepared to live with the new rates provided that they don't exceed 20%," noted Wendy Cutler, senior vice president at the Asia Society Policy Institute.

    Recent findings suggest that by retaining the option to raise levies if bilateral talks deteriorate, Washington is using the tariffs as leverage to "secure expected shipments of critical minerals and rare earths, and further purchases of U.S. agricultural goods," Cutler said.

    Washington has warned that tariffs on Chinese goods could double to 40% if the USTR finds that Beijing is not engaging. "If the trade war did start up again, today's measures provide the U.S. with some ammunition," Williams remarked.

    Even the sweeping actions against the other 13 trading partners appear aimed squarely at China, stated Williams, who tallied that the word "China" appears 253 times in the USTR's report on Vietnam, and 315 times in the document on the European Union.

    "Foremost among the 'unreasonable acts, policies, and practices' that these countries are criticised for is being slow to restrict imports and FDI from China," Williams stated.

    While the proposed tariffs generally lift average rates only modestly, India and Vietnam stand out because of the wider gaps between the rates they would face with and without a deal, analysts said.

    India and Vietnam face proposed tariffs of 25% and 35%, respectively, but those rates could fall sharply to 17% and 20% if ongoing talks with the U.S. produce reciprocal trade agreements.

    The two countries have "a strong incentive" to conclude deals with Washington to secure the lower rates, Cutler mentioned.

    In a recent development, vietnam's trade ministry said Thursday that it was working with the U.S. to complete a trade deal as soon as possible, according to Reuters. India could also gain an edge over some Asian rivals through comparatively lower levies if New Delhi concludes its long-pending trade deal with Washington.

    Singapore faces a similar challenge. The proposal sets a maximum potential rate of 20% on its exports, net of existing Section 301 tariffs, which could fall to 10% if it reaches an agreement on reciprocal trade with the U.S. or concludes other negotiations addressing the USTR's findings, according to Singapore's Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry.

    The ministry said it disagreed with the findings and was "very disappointed" with the proposed action, arguing that it failed to account for the structure of Singapore's economy.

    It has been revealed that speaking to reporters, Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong said that about 33%, or 9.4 billion Singapore dollars ($7.2 billion) of direct exports will be affected, and the effective tariff rate on affected Singapore exports will rise to 10.3% from the current 7.8%, should Washington impose the highest levy of 20%. "I'm also very surprised that this has happened because this is not something that you would expect from an important major trading partner," Gan added, saying "We have been working together for many years, and we have an FTA with the U.S.," Gan said, referring to the U.S.-Singapore Free Trade Agreement that was in force since 2004.

    Under the FTA, Singapore imposes zero tariffs on U.S. goods, while the U.S. has run a trade surplus with the city-state for more than 20 years, the ministry said. That surplus grew to $33 billion in 2025 from $27 billion in 2024.

    Singapore noted it would submit further comments during the public consultation period and urge the USTR to reconsider.

    Exemptions for semiconductors and other electronics should cushion the impact on South Korea and Taiwan, whose economies are heavily concentrated in those sectors, analysts said.

    Sources indicate that the USTR singled out South Korea for its concentration in memory-chip production and what it described as outsized government support. Yet it excluded the country's chips from the proposed excess-capacity tariffs.

    It has been revealed that taiwan, which faces an excess-capacity tariff cap of 15%, also benefits from exemptions for other electronics, including mobile phones and networking equipment. Its effective tariff rate would rise to about 9% from 6%, Williams estimated.

    In a recent development, switzerland was hit with a shock 39% tariff rate back in 2025, targeting significant exports, from chemicals and pharmaceuticals to gold, watches and chocolates. In November 2025, it negotiated a deal that slashed U.S. duties to 15% in return for a commitment to invest billions and increase manufacturing Stateside.

    It has been revealed that in March 2026, the U.S. launched further Section 301 investigations into Switzerland over "unfair or discriminatory trade practices," landing on a recommendation to impose an additional 15% tariff.

    Switzerland's Economy Ministry told CNBC that the country rejected the allegations raised during the investigations and remarked it had already presented its arguments during bilateral consultations with the U.S. Treasury.

    Industry observers note that the ministry added that it assumed the latest recommendation was consistent with the deal struck in November 2025 and said it was in close contact with U.S. authorities as it reviews next steps.

    According to recent reports, officials for both Switzerland and the European Union remarked during trade discussions last year that while they had a trade surplus with Washington in goods, the relationship was balanced when accounting for both trade and services, where the U.S. dominates in areas such as technology and finance.

    Industry observers note that brussels noted it was assessing the U.S. report but rejected its finding that Europe was a source of industrial overcapacity.

    "To the contrary, Europe is among those most exposed to overcapacity," European Commission Spokesperson Olof Gill said in a statement.

    "The EU and the U.S. share a real concern about global overcapacity, much of it state-driven and concentrated in third countries. We regret the lack of joint action," Gill stated.

    The EU expects any measure taken from the investigation to respect the existing joint agreement of a 15% all-inclusive ceiling on EU goods, Gill added.

    EU trade ministers are due to speak with U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer on Monday.

    Citi analysts noted they expected a hit on European retailers if the measures stay as unveiled, with the likes of Adidas, H&M, Puma and Primark potentially seeing downgrades on full-year 2027 earnings.

    Inga Fechner, senior economist for global trade at ING, stated in a Wednesday note that the U.S. "tariff wall keeps changing, but it isn't coming down," adding that "U.S. protectionism is becoming increasingly difficult to unwind.".

    While the newly Democrat-controlled Congress could try to restrict presidential tariff authority, remove individual duties or apply greater scrutiny via hearings and investigations, actually reversing the measures will be difficult while Trump retains veto power, she said.

    "We don't think the blue wave will mark a return to free trade. The Biden years already highlighted that tariffs in strategically vital sectors enjoy support across political camps.".

    Protectionist moves become more targeted, she added, adding to a complex system of country- and sector-specific duties based on different legal authorities.

    — CNBC's Evelyn Cheng contributed to this report.

    Tech German software major SAP is reportedly weighing cutting at least 10,000 jobs in AI push

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (432 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • SAP is preparing a proposal to eliminate at least 10,000 positions as the German firm reshapes its software business for the artificial intelligence era, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.
    • The report came as the company flagged a cybersecurity attack, but noted it had found "no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data.".
    • "SAP has identified suspicious activity and promptly implemented the necessary measures to protect its customers and preserve the security of its services," a manufacturer spokesperson said.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    SAP is preparing a proposal to eliminate at least 10,000 positions as the German firm reshapes its software business for the artificial intelligence era, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

    The report came as the company flagged a cybersecurity attack, but noted it had found "no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data.".

    "SAP has identified suspicious activity and promptly implemented the necessary measures to protect its customers and preserve the security of its services," a manufacturer spokesperson said.

    It has been revealed that "Our customers trust us to protect their data, and that remains our highest priority. In a highly dynamic threat environment, we will continue to strengthen our security to provide the secure and resilient environment our customers depend on.".

    The tech giant did not respond to a request for comment on the reported job cuts. The number could change after labor negotiations.

    Recent findings suggest that other software companies have also tied workforce reductions to AI initiatives, though for different reasons. WiseTech Global remarked in February it planned to cut about 2,000 jobs over two years as it integrated AI into its products and operations.

    Atlassian said in March it would cut about 1,600 jobs partly to fund further AI investment, while Cloudflare said in May it would eliminate more than 1,100 roles as it moved toward an AI-first operating model.

    In the U.S., employers cited AI in 121,401 job-cut announcements through October 2026, accounting for about 20% of the total, according to a Nov. 5 report from outplacement and executive coaching firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas.

    In a recent development, SAP employs more than 110,000 people worldwide. Bloomberg reported that all departments had been asked to identify potential cuts, with product, engineering and sales in particular focus.

    The company also underwent a reorganization in 2024, when it eliminated around 10,000 positions through a program that relied mainly on voluntary departures and retraining.

    Its headcount later remained relatively flat as it hired for newly introduced roles, Bloomberg reported.

    In 2023, SAP CEO Christian Klein told CNBC he did not necessarily expect a reduction in the workforce, saying he expected the company to grow and "accelerate" its total revenue.

    Recent findings suggest that the reported cuts come as Klein pushes SAP toward an AI-first strategy. This year, SAP completed four acquisitions — Reltio, Dremio, Prior Labs and TechWolf — and made strategic investments in AI-focused companies including Parloa, n8n and Conduct.

    The acquisitions are intended to help SAP organize company data, develop AI models for business information and analyze workforce skills.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • President Donald Trump on Thursday falsely deemed the latest gross domestic product revision a mistake, claiming that it should be "immediately investigated.".
    • Data released Wednesday from the Commerce Department revealed that the U.S.
    • That revision was a "RECORD SETTING ERROR," Trump said in a Truth Social post, suggesting that the initial release could have influenced the outcome of the 2026 U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    President Donald Trump on Thursday falsely deemed the latest gross domestic product revision a mistake, claiming that it should be "immediately investigated.".

    Data released Wednesday from the Commerce Department revealed that the U.S. economy exhibited much stronger growth for the third quarter than initially estimated, showing that real GDP grew at a 4.3% annualized rate. That was revised upward from the department's advance estimate of 3.4%.

    That revision was a "RECORD SETTING ERROR," Trump said in a Truth Social post, suggesting that the initial release could have influenced the outcome of the 2026 U.S. midterm elections, where Democrats flipped both chambers of Congress and even multiple governorships.

    "I would like to wish a Happy Thanksgiving to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%, A RECORD SETTING ERROR, and one so grave that it should be immediately investigated," Trump wrote.

    However, the difference between the advance estimate and the figure in the second release is far from being an all-time record. It was the largest revision since the 1.2 percentage point revision seen in the second quarter of 2020.

    On an absolute basis, the latest revision was tied for 16th among all revisions from the advance estimate to the second release since 1990. It also tied four other quarters with a similar 0.9 percentage point difference — and was approximately double the average revision of 0.43 percentage points for all 147 quarters.

    The upward revision highlights Trump's policies are "delivering results" that defy expectations, White House spokesman Matthew Middleton told CNBC.

    According to recent reports, revisions to U.S. economic numbers are not out of the ordinary. Initial reports count on partial survey data and early estimates. Those data are later updated with more survey responses — which sometimes leads to changes from the initial reports.

    GDP data is revised repeatedly over a five year period. By the time the final revision is done, the average absolute error from the second release to the final is 1.14 percentage points.

    According to recent reports, the advance estimate for Q3 U.S. GDP, which came just days before Election Day in early November, was still better than the figure economists had expected at the time. It also revealed a significant step-up in growth from the second quarter.

    Because that was a strong showing for the economy, some on Wall Street consider this week's revision to be a confirmation of the economy's recent growth trend.

    Jim Baird of Plante Moran Financial Advisors said immediately following the release that it "reinforces an increasingly familiar tension" that the economy is "performing quite well, but its resilience also gives the Fed an even stronger case for further rate hikes.".

    "The economy isn't merely hanging in there. It continues to demonstrate considerable resilience, with consumers spending, businesses investing and few signs that restrictive monetary policy is creating significant cracks in the broader expansion," the firm's chief investment officer said.

    Traders are presently pricing in a nearly 100% chance of a hike at the Federal Open Market Committee's December meeting, per the CME FedWatch tool. They're also anticipating an additional hike in January.

    — CNBC's Jeff Cox and Fred Imbert contributed reporting.

    Industry observers note that in response, a spokesperson for Iran's military told state media that no offensive or military operations had been carried out in the area and that "these accusations should be viewed as a cover for continued malevolence and an attempt to exacerbate insecurity in the region" by U.S. and Israeli forces.

    Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Telegram that he had spoken with his Italian counterpart, Antonio Tajani, and expressed regret over their deaths, while stressing that Tehran had no role or involvement in the incident.

    "The incident is suspicious and looks like a precooked recipe for war," Araghchi wrote on X.

    He also said Iran was ready to cooperate with the governments of Kuwait and Italy in investigating the incident.

    Sources indicate that separately, Israel noted Thursday that it was prepared to carry out strikes against Iran "at any moment," even without U.S. forces joining the effort, according to Israeli military spokesman Effie Defrin on Israeli broadcaster Kan.

    The comments came after U.S. envoy Jared Kushner told a podcast Wednesday that Israel "needs to get out of the constant wartime mindset.".

    Israel has been pushing the Trump administration to back another offensive against Tehran, with Reuters reporting on Nov. 18 that Israeli spy chief Roman Gofman pushed for joint strikes when he met U.S. officials earlier in the month.

    Industry observers note that late Thursday, President Donald Trump said on PBS that the U.S. had "victory at hand" in the Iran conflict and reiterated that victory would come "whenever I want it to be, to be honest.".

    Sources indicate that speaking during a Thanksgiving call with U.S. military personnel, Trump said Washington was still trying to give Iran "every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives.".

    But he added that he was not sure whether Tehran would agree.

    In a recent development, "Some people question why. Are they crazy? Maybe they are," Trump stated.

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (970 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Nvidia's billion-dollar board bet: Who's protected as lawsuits mount?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (970 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jensen Huang is back as CEO of Nvidia, after President Donald Trump urged the manufacturer's board to rehire Huang.
    • Industry observers note that "Clearly they caved to external pressure," stated Betsy Atkins, an author and longtime public-tech giant director.
    • Recent findings suggest that california Attorney General Rob Bonta is investigating whether Nvidia misrepresented information to investors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang is back as CEO of Nvidia, after President Donald Trump urged the manufacturer's board to rehire Huang. But investigations into the company, its executive leadership and its board continue as outside criticism mounts.

    Industry observers note that "Clearly they caved to external pressure," stated Betsy Atkins, an author and longtime public-tech giant director. "The board failed," she said, when it initially allowed Huang's removal. "The board's role is to think of all stakeholders.".

    Recent findings suggest that california Attorney General Rob Bonta is investigating whether Nvidia misrepresented information to investors. "There is classic corporate securities law on the books in California that prevents investors and the public from being misled by companies," Bonta noted on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Tuesday.

    It has been revealed that directors are already defendants in a shareholder lawsuit accusing them of failing to oversee Nvidia. A separate securities class action targets the company and Huang, its co-founder.

    In a recent development, now the board’s insurance choices are part of the story. A risk advisor with direct knowledge of Nvidia’s coverage says the manufacturer built an approximately $1 billion D&O tower, insurance jargon for directors and officers insurance policies from different companies that combine to cover one massive risk.

    In a recent development, nvidia "loves insurance," the advisor noted. “They buy insurance as if they have no balance sheet.” A billion-dollar tower would essentially mean Nvidia "bought the market," purchasing all the coverage it could get, according to an industry expert with 25 years working in financial insurance. The expert asked not to be named out of concern for past or potential future clients.

    Sources indicate that but Nvidia directed all that coverage to Side A only, according to CNBC's source. Side A protects directors and officers personally when the company cannot indemnify them. Side B covers the company for legal defense costs or settlements on behalf of directors and officers, and Side C protects the company when it's named as a defendant in a suit such as a securities claim.

    The risk advisor says Nvidia believed it had "the war chest" to protect itself against a securities class action suit.

    According to recent reports, that choice is raising questions about whether the board protected itself at the tech giant’s expense. CNBC asked Nvidia for comment but received no response.

    An insurance CEO characterized a billion-dollar policy as a lot of coverage, but noted a Side A-only allocation was a surprising move because it results in imbalanced coverage, protecting only directors.

    Recent findings suggest that that structure is not automatically a governance failure, according to a D&O insurance expert with long experience in coverage for banks, drugmakers and other businesses that often face litigation. Side A-only programs are common among companies with the capital to manage the corporate risk internally.

    "For a organization with Nvidia’s resources, retaining the company-side risk can make financial sense," the advisor said. It's Side A D&O that's "imperative to corporate governance.".

    "It is a capital-allocation decision," the expert told me. The firm decides that buying insurance for its own balance sheet is not worth the premium. In other words, Side B and Side C are considered too expensive for the coverage the company gets.

    The question for shareholders is whether the board’s decision to hold that risk was a sound use of the tech giant’s resources and whether the company can absorb the costs if the claims grow.

    A shareholder derivative complaint filed Nov. 11 names Huang, directors and other officers. It alleges that they failed to oversee risks involving Huang’s relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang and made misleading statements. It also alleges that some defendants sold roughly $2 billion in Nvidia stock while holding material nonpublic information. Those remain allegations, not findings.

    According to recent reports, A separate securities class action, filed Nov. 9, names Nvidia and Huang. It seeks damages for investors who bought Nvidia shares between Oct. 9, 2025, and Nov. 8, 2026, alleging the organization and Huang misled investors.

    The distinction matters: The derivative suit is brought on Nvidia’s behalf, while the class action seeks recovery for investors.

    Industry observers note that "Insurance is already at work," indicates Michel Léonard, chief economist at the Insurance Information Institute, describing standard policy mechanics, not Nvidia’s specific policy. "Once the suit is filed, D&O starts paying defense costs, long before anyone proves anything.".

    A claim still has to meet the policy’s terms, and defense costs can reduce the remaining limits. Nor does a drop in Nvidia’s market value by itself establish an insurable loss. Plaintiffs would need to prove legally recoverable damages; the policy would respond only to covered losses.

    In a recent development, the board has already taken steps it indicates are aimed at accountability. Nvidia announced an independent investigation on Nov. 8, and independent directors retained outside counsel two days later. Huang resigned as CEO and a director on Nov. 11; the board appointed CFO Colette Kress interim CEO. Nvidia said it had no reason to believe national security or manufacturer secrets had been compromised by Huang's extramarital relationships.

    According to recent reports, atkins, who joined the board of Wynn Resorts in 2018 after founder Steve Wynn resigned, argues that allegations are not conclusions and that boards should also weigh governance concerns against the value a founder brings to a organization’s innovation. Nvidia's investigation is continuing even as Huang resumes leadership.

    “Will companies’ hyper-accelerated innovation speed be the same without them? I don’t think so,” noted Atkins, author of "Don't Waste a Board Seat: A Decision-Maker's Guide to Choosing Directors Who Create Value.".

    Nvidia’s 2026 proxy also says the company has indemnity agreements with its directors and officers — separate from its insurance. Those agreements provide for the company to cover certain costs and liabilities when the law permits.

    #142202. Sovereign wealth funds are acting more like private equity giants — and inheriting their risks

    📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (947 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Sovereign wealth funds are acting more like private equity giants — and inheriting their risks

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (947 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that for decades, sovereign wealth funds were among private equity's most deep-pocketed backers, entrusting billions of dollars to buyout firms to invest on their behalf.
    • From originating transactions and taking controlling stakes in companies to building their own investment platforms, some of the world's largest state investors are adopting the playbook of traditional private equity giants, according to industry veterans.
    • It has been revealed that "The imminent change is that the lines between LPs and GPs are becoming increasingly blurry.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that for decades, sovereign wealth funds were among private equity's most deep-pocketed backers, entrusting billions of dollars to buyout firms to invest on their behalf. Increasingly, they are doing the dealmaking themselves.

    From originating transactions and taking controlling stakes in companies to building their own investment platforms, some of the world's largest state investors are adopting the playbook of traditional private equity giants, according to industry veterans.

    It has been revealed that "The imminent change is that the lines between LPs and GPs are becoming increasingly blurry. This could bring more fundamental changes in the long term," Diego Lopez of Global SWF told CNBC.

    Limited partners, or LPs, typically commit capital to private equity funds, while general partners, or GPs, are responsible for sourcing deals and managing investments.

    Sovereign funds and state investment companies are increasingly taking on the GP role, Lopez mentioned, pointing to the establishment of their own private equity management platforms, such as Mubadala Capital and Singapore's Seviora.

    The shift is also reflected in the way some of the world's largest sovereign investors are approaching dealmaking.

    Recent findings suggest that "They originate transactions rather than waiting for them. They build platforms rather than buying single assets. They take control positions and operate what they own," PwC said in their latest report on sovereign wealth funds.

    "Whether you're a company, a general partner, or a government, you'll find that these institutions are no longer the limited partner you're raising money from; they're the principal sitting across the table.".

    Industry observers note that last year, Abu Dhabi's MGX, an investment vehicle established by state fund Mubadala in 2024, anchored the roughly $40 billion acquisition of Aligned Data Centers alongside BlackRock, Nvidia and Microsoft. A year earlier, a consortium led by Mubadala Capital acquired a 68% equity stake in alternative asset manager Fortress, which at the time managed more than $48 billion.

    Some sovereign funds are striking deals at a speed typically associated with large private equity firms, according to PwC.

    Singapore's GIC recorded 553 transactions between July 2023 and July 2026, Abu Dhabi's Mubadala 397 and the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority 367, according to PwC's analysis of PitchBook data, which includes transactions by subsidiaries.

    The shift comes as sovereign wealth funds command unprecedented financial firepower. Their assets have surged about 59% over the past five years to $16.5 trillion, up from $10.4 trillion in 2022 and more than nine times the $1.8 trillion they managed in 2005, according to data provided to CNBC by research firm Global SWF which focuses on state-owned investors.

    PwC projects that sovereign wealth fund assets to reach $22.4 trillion by 2030.

    While sovereign funds' push into direct investing has been underway for years, a more challenging fundraising environment for PE firms and a resurgence in megadeals have recently accelerated the trend.

    The fundraising slowdown has tilted bargaining power toward large institutional investors, allowing them to negotiate more opportunities to invest directly alongside private equity managers, remarked Kyle Walters of PitchBook.

    Industry observers note that A key attraction is the potential to save on fees. Co-investments typically carry little or no management fees and no carried interest, which is the share of investment profits that managers receive. Additionally, direct deals can eliminate external manager fees altogether.

    "For a large SWF writing big checks, the fee savings in dollar terms can be substantial," Walters stated.

    Industry observers note that sovereign funds also enjoy structural advantages over traditional buyout firms. Unlike conventional private equity funds, which operate within predetermined lifespans, sovereign investors can hold assets for decades, the experts highlighted.

    They can also deploy substantial sums from their own balance sheets without having to raise fresh capital, an advantage particularly valuable in capital-intensive sectors such as AI infrastructure and energy.

    But deep pockets and patient capital alone do not guarantee success.

    As sovereign wealth funds take controlling stakes in companies, they assume operational responsibilities traditionally borne by private equity managers, while potentially stretching their own capacity to source deals, conduct due diligence and manage complex assets, PwC cautioned.

    "Building the required capability, the talent, the systems, and the governance is a slower process than committing the capital," PwC remarked. The firm also flagged concentration risks as sovereign investors increasingly pile into similar investment themes, particularly AI, data centers and power infrastructure, leaving even geographically diversified portfolios vulnerable to the same underlying risks.

    Despite their growing ambitions, industry experts are skeptical that sovereign wealth funds will supplant established private equity managers.

    "This latest path these large LPs are paving is more of a partnership than a competition between GPs and LPs," Walters said, noting that much of the increased activity is taking the form of co-investments.

    He pointed to the $55 billion take-private deal for video-game maker Electronic Arts revealed last year, in which Saudi Arabia's PIF contributed significant capital, as an example of how both sides ae joining hands.

    Traditional buyout firms also retain an edge in sourcing deals and managing portfolio companies.

    "However, capital alone does not replace the specialist sourcing, operational expertise, and active ownership capabilities required to consistently create value, which experienced managers have built over time," mentioned Vincent Ng, managing director and co-head of Asia at Partners Group.

    Direct investing also raises concentration risks, while illiquidity could become a problem during crises when governments need access to capital, experts noted.

    Rather than displacing traditional buyout firms, sovereign investors' growing ambitions could change the economics of private equity, forcing managers to become more flexible in how they work with their biggest clients.

    "This is likely to reshape the relationship between asset owners and managers, with more customized mandates, co-investments, and long-term partnerships," Ng stated.

    #142199. Semiconductor chips are the new oil. Here's why

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (520 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Semiconductor chips are the new oil. Here's why

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (520 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The artificial intelligence boom has pushed semiconductors past oil and gas in global export value for the first time, according to a Deutsche Bank analysis of International Trade Centre data.
    • Sources indicate that yet the milestone arrives at an awkward moment, just as investors reassess the outlook for artificial intelligence spending and drive down the price of semiconductor stocks.
    • Industry observers note that nvidia soared more than 31% Monday after the leading maker of artificial intelligence chips had fallen for a seventh straight week, plunging 46% during that stretch.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The artificial intelligence boom has pushed semiconductors past oil and gas in global export value for the first time, according to a Deutsche Bank analysis of International Trade Centre data.

    Sources indicate that yet the milestone arrives at an awkward moment, just as investors reassess the outlook for artificial intelligence spending and drive down the price of semiconductor stocks. Last week, before Monday's breathtaking reversal, semiconductor stocks suffered their worst weekly loss in a quarter century, with the PHLX Semiconductor Index (SOX) plunging nearly 11% last Friday alone, capping a more than 17% weekly decline.

    Industry observers note that nvidia soared more than 31% Monday after the leading maker of artificial intelligence chips had fallen for a seventh straight week, plunging 46% during that stretch. Then it fell again, dropping almost 10% on Tuesday and Wednesday. Advanced Micro Devices tumbled 20% in two days last Thursday and Friday. Micron Technology sank 27% over the seven days ended last Friday.

    According to recent reports, "For decades we've talked about the petrodollar. Perhaps increasingly we need to think about the chip dollar," Jim Reid, global head of macro and thematic research at Deutsche Bank wrote in a report this month.

    Semiconductor exports overtook oil and gas for the first time during the January-March quarter of 2026, reaching about $1.61 trillion, compared with $1.53 trillion for oil and gas, the report stated, using four-quarter rolling totals.

    The gap widened in the second quarter, when semiconductor exports totaled about $1.60 trillion and oil and gas exports reached about $1.47 trillion. Disruptions to oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz after the Iran war helped widen the gap. Daily oil flows through the Strait collapsed nearly 77%, to 4.9 million barrels in the second quarter of 2026 from 21.6 million barrels in the fourth quarter of 2025, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

    Yet the demand for semiconductors has proven insatiable in the face of soaring data center construction, boosting global trade in the increasingly scarce AI component. Hundreds of billions of dollars of orders for graphics processing units and data centers aim at providing AI computing power, Rothschild & Co. Redburn wrote in a report last Thursday.

    "Compute will be the new commodity fueling this transformation on a global scale," Rothschild analyst Cara Thomson remarked.

    The shift toward chips has macroeconomic implications just as the explosion in oil trade did in the 1970s.

    Industry observers note that oil-exporting countries historically recycled much of their surpluses into the purchase of U.S. Treasuries and other bonds, helping finance U.S. deficits and underpin demand for other government debt.

    Reid at Deutsche Bank mentioned that since semiconductor-surplus countries in Asia are more closely tied to U.S. tech companies, some chip-export earnings could flow back into U.S. technology stocks, startups and data centers, further helping to finance the AI investment cycle.

    Industry observers note that the changing dynamics in global trade could also tilt the mix of global financial flows, Reid remarked. "So welcome to the chip-dollar era: potentially more growth, more excitement, more volatility, and structurally higher yields" in corporate and government debt.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

    It has been revealed that that made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

    As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

    When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

    According to recent reports, not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

    In a recent development, loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

    It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

    Recent findings suggest that our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

    Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

    Recent findings suggest that look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

    Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

    Industry observers note that finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an glitch is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that emotions were high following the Philadelphia Eagles' comeback win over the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving. Especially for Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni.

    The immediate aftermath of the game saw Sirianni approach a group of field-level Eagles fans and exchange some high-fives, before looking at another group and getting pulled back by a pair of staffers. It's unclear what happened, but Sirianni appeared to maintain eye contact with someone and tried to force his way back before getting pulled to the field.

    It was only a few seconds, but it drew attention on social media.

    Sources indicate that the simple explanation appeared to be Sirianni, who wears his heart on his sleeve in the best of times, was trying to get into it with the opposing fan base. The team and coach are claiming that wasn't the case.

    While speaking with reporters postgame, Sirianni remarked he was only trying to celebrate with Eagles fans and that he was pulled back to the field to shake hands with Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer:.

    Recent findings suggest that "There were a lot of Eagles fans back there, I was excited to celebrate with those Eagles fans and our team and everything like that. It was fun … I'm sure there were some [Cowboys fans] in there but at that point it felt like there was only Eagles fans, we were able to high-five.

    "I had to shake everybody's hand out on the field and wanted to be able to celebrate with everybody, and also shake Schotty's hands and their players' hands.".

    In a recent development, an Eagles representative apparently backed up this account with Pro Football Talk, contending that Sirianni was only celebrating. We'll see if anything else comes of that, but Sirianni is the head coach with less to worry about following that game.

    Industry observers note that philadelphia's win went down as the biggest comeback in NFL Thanksgiving history. The Cowboys led 28-10 at halftime and by as many as 21 points late in the third quarter, only for a superb performance by former Cowboys practice-squad QB Joe Milton, now playing for the Eagles, and some brutal mistakes by Dallas to trigger a wild comeback.

    Eagles kicker Jake Elliott made a 59-yard field goal for the win, improving the Eagles' record to 4-7 in what has been a trying season for a team that won a Super Bowl less than two years ago.
